question: The navigable portion of Barak River in India is the 121 km stretch between Lakhipur and Bhanga, which was declared in the year 2016.
solution:
The correct answer is __**NW-16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NW-16**, or National Waterway-16, refers to the navigable stretch of the Barak River in India.
 
• The Barak River's 121 km stretch between Lakhipur and Bhanga in Assam was declared a national waterway in **2016** under the National Waterways Act, 2016.
 
• This waterway facilitates inland water transportation and promotes trade and connectivity in Northeast India.
 
• The development of NW-16 aims to connect Assam with the neighboring regions and improve the logistics infrastructure in the area.
 
• NW-16 is managed and maintained by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**, which oversees the development of inland waterways in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Waterways Act, 2016:**

 
 
• The Act was passed to declare 111 rivers across India as national waterways.
 
• It aims to develop inland water transport as a sustainable and economical mode of transportation.
 
• The waterway system supports cargo movement and reduces road congestion and environmental pollution.
 
 
 
• **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI):**
 
 
• Established in 1986, IWAI is responsible for the development and regulation of inland waterways in India.
 
• It oversees the maintenance of navigable channels, terminals, and related infrastructure.
 
• IWAI promotes multimodal transportation and connectivity by integrating waterways with rail and road systems.
 
 
 
• **Barak River:**
 
 
• The Barak River is one of the major rivers in Northeast India, flowing through Assam, Manipur, and Mizoram.
 
• It serves as a vital waterway for the region, supporting trade, agriculture, and livelihood.
 
• The river eventually flows into Bangladesh, joining the Meghna River system.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Inland Waterways:**
 
 
• Inland waterways are a cost-effective and eco-friendly mode of transportation.
 
• They reduce dependency on road and rail infrastructure, lowering logistics costs.
 
• The development of waterways boosts regional trade, tourism, and economic growth.
